title: Source Record
description: Two related shapes for a research source, distinguished by $id fragment via oneOf-free convention — see the two definitions below. 'input' is one element of the JSONB array passed to collect_research_sources() (already provider-normalized by the calling n8n workflow, before dedup/scoring). 'stored' is a row of the `sources` table as returned by get_current_research_package(). See docs/architecture/research-pipeline.md#web-search--source-collection.

published_at.description: Provider-returned date/timestamp string, precision varies (date-only or full timestamp) -- stored as-is; the `sources.published_at` column is TIMESTAMPTZ, so Postgres normalizes/validates it on insert rather than this schema enforcing one format.

excerpt.description: Short relevant excerpt/snippet only — never a full-article dump.

provider_relevance.description: Search-provider-reported relevance score, 0-1, if the provider returns one.

raw_metadata.description: Provider-specific fields worth keeping, safe-fields-only (no credential values).

published_at.description: Provider-returned date/timestamp string, precision varies (date-only or full timestamp) -- stored as-is; the `sources.published_at` column is TIMESTAMPTZ, so Postgres normalizes/validates it on insert rather than this schema enforcing one format.
